issues_detected.description: No processing software carries a version anywhere in the record and no software_and_tools slot is used. The conversion pipelines the record itself describes (.fda and .sdt to DICOM, .FIT to Open mHealth, device-native .xml for ECG to WFDB) name no tool at all. Capture and QC software is identifiable only indirectly: REDCap, the MoCA Duo application, the OMOP CDM Data Quality Dashboard implied by dqd_omop.json, and the project GitHub organization https://github.com/AI-READI listed as an external resource.
issues_detected.recommendation: Name the conversion tools with versions and link the specific AI-READI GitHub repositories used for each pipeline, rather than leaving the transformation agentless.

issues_detected.description: data_protection_impacts is absent and no data protection impact statement appears anywhere in the record, not even as a truthful negative. The record documents human subjects, HIPAA Safe Harbor de-identification, a theoretical re-identification risk and watermarking, all of which are the inputs a DPIA would consume, so a reader cannot tell whether an impact assessment was conducted, was declined, or was simply not extracted. Sibling AI_READI records carry the source's 'no data protection impact analysis has been conducted' statement in notes or in the slot itself.
issues_detected.recommendation: Populate data_protection_impacts with the source's DPIA status, including an explicit 'not conducted' where that is what the documentation states.

issues_detected.description: Two distinct institutions appear for the study's home. data_governance.accountable_organization, the license Licensor and the principal investigator's affiliation are Washington University in St. Louis (ROR:01yc7t268), while the reviewing IRB, its hsdrely@uw.edu contact and the NIH RePORTER awardee for OT2OD032644 are the University of Washington (ROR:00cvxb145). The record declares the conflict in record-level source_caveats, on the principal_investigator entry and on the ethical_reviews entry, and states that both tier-1 statements are reported rather than reconciled.
issues_detected.recommendation: Reconcile upstream against NIH RePORTER and the IRB record; the per-slot caveats are the correct interim treatment and should be kept until the sources agree.

issues_detected.description: parent_datasets, was_derived_from and errata are absent although the underlying information is present elsewhere. related_datasets records is_new_version_of for both doi:10.60775/fairhub.1 and doi:10.60775/fairhub.2 plus a has_part relation to the mini-subset, distribution_dates and version_access carry the per-release chain with dates and participant counts, and the version 3.0.0 removal of the Snellen visual-acuity variables is recorded as a quality_note on a variable rather than as an erratum.
issues_detected.recommendation: Mirror the two predecessor releases into parent_datasets and was_derived_from, and record the Snellen variable removal as an erratum so lineage and corrections are machine-readable in the provenance slots.

issues_detected.description: Only 7 keywords are supplied, against 9 to 10 in sibling AI_READI records from the same pipeline family. The list carries the condition, two AI terms and four modality terms, but omits the program identifier (Bridge2AI, AI-READI), the salutogenesis framing, and several modalities the description enumerates at length: optical coherence tomography, OCT angiography, fluorescence lifetime imaging ophthalmoscopy, wearable activity monitoring and home environmental sensing. Discoverability is narrower than the described content.
issues_detected.recommendation: Extend keywords to cover the program, the salutogenesis framing and the OCT/OCTA/FLIO/wearable/environmental modalities the description already names.

issues_detected.description: The race/ethnicity and biological sex subpopulation entries set subpopulation_elements_present: false while populating distribution with aggregate counts from the release summary table (380/545/519/836 and 951/1329). The identification text explains that the variables are used for recruitment balance but withheld from the public release, so the encoding is documented, but the boolean and the populated distribution read against each other for any consumer that reads the flag alone.
issues_detected.recommendation: State in the identification text, or via a per-set flag, that only aggregate counts are public and no participant-level variable is released.

issues_detected.description: The NIH project period recorded for OT2OD032644 ends 2025-08-31, yet the version 3.0.0 release date is 2025-11-17, the anticipated study completion is 2027-01-01, recruitment is reported in the collection_timeframes caveat as continuing to 2026-11-30, and updates commits to approximately annual future releases. No continuation award or no-cost extension is named. Raw-data preservation is committed only 'at least for the duration of the project'.
issues_detected.recommendation: Document the continuation mechanism supporting activity past 2025-08-31 and a preservation commitment that outlives the award period.

issues_detected.description: publisher is populated with the platform URL 'https://fairhub.io/' rather than the platform name, and the flat license slot carries the license name 'AI-READI custom license v2.0' rather than a URI, although the license DOI (10.5281/zenodo.17555036) is present in license_and_use_terms and in external_resources. Both are internally consistent with citation and license_and_use_terms; the objection is to the form of the value, not to its truth.
issues_detected.recommendation: Record publisher as the named platform (FAIRhub) with the URL as its id, and put the license DOI in the license slot.

issues_detected.description: The nine per-directory total_bytes values sum to 3,815,969,360,064 against the stated total_size_bytes of 3,815,969,779,678, a shortfall of 419,614 bytes. The record declares the shortfall in source_caveats and attributes it to the root-level metadata directory, whose file_count is enumerated but whose total_bytes is deliberately left unpopulated because no source states it. The discrepancy is therefore disclosed and explained, not silent.
issues_detected.recommendation: No correction needed; optionally record the root metadata directory's byte total once a source states it.

issues_detected.description: DOI prefix 10.60775 (FAIRhub) is well-formed and used consistently for id, doi, the three-release version chain and every file_collection identifier fragment, but is not a widely catalogued registrar prefix and was not independently resolved here.
issues_detected.recommendation: No change needed; the prefix is consistent with the FAIRhub landing page https://fairhub.io/datasets/3 given in page.

semantic_insights: File-count arithmetic reconciles exactly: the ten file_collections file_count values sum to 356,343, matching total_file_count, and the record's own source_caveats explains the reconciliation by enumerating the nine root-level metadata files (CHANGELOG.md, dataset_description.json, dataset_structure_description.json, healthsheet.md, LICENSE.txt, participants.json, participants.tsv, README.md, study_description.json) that the nine data-type directories do not contain.

Every participant count reconciles to 2,280: race/ethnicity 380+545+519+836, biological sex 951+1,329, diabetes status 776+560+686+258, and the recommended split 1,576+352+352 at the stated 70/15/15 proportions.

Grant numbers follow NIH format (OT2OD032644, P30DK035816, UL1TR003096); OT2OD032644 carries the RePORTER project number 1OT2OD032644-01 with award amount and project period, and the funders.source_caveats explains why grants named only in tier-3 publications are retained alongside the single tier-1 funding reference.

The de-identification account is unusually precise rather than smoothed over: FAIRhub's 'NoDeIdentification' (no identifiers collected), the RO-Crate's deidentified flag and the HIPAA Safe Harbor stripping of the public set are all carried in is_deidentified with the reason each source gives, and the internal-review-only status ('has not undergone any formal external audit') is stated.

conforms_to_standard carries seven controlled values (CDS, WFDB, OMOP_CDM, DICOM, OPEN_MHEALTH, ESDS, RO_CRATE) and every file_collection repeats the pair that applies to it, so format conformance is asserted per directory rather than only at the dataset level.

The public/controlled distinction is applied consistently across description, sensitive_elements, is_deidentified.identifiers_removed, informed_consent.consent_scope, raw_data_sources.access_details and data_governance.access_review_process; the same four withheld variable groups (sex, race/ethnicity, medications, plus zip code, genetic data, past health records and traffic reports) appear in each place.

All four known_biases entries carry BiasTypeEnum values (selection_bias twice, representation_bias, sampling_bias) and three of the four pair the bias with a mitigation_strategy; the English-language selection bias is the one entry with no mitigation recorded.

sampling_strategies resolves a genuine source conflict rather than picking a side: the healthsheet's 'contains all possible instances' is scoped to the data cut-off while the study's own 'Non-Probability Sample' characterization is applied to the health-system population, and both are stated in notes.

Confidentiality is reasoned rather than copied: other_compliance records the RO-Crate's 'HL7:2N (normal)' value and explains that confidentiality_level is set to restricted because access is gated by verified-ID login and license assent.

The 20 collection_mechanisms entries name device make, model and acquisition parameters (Philips PageWriter TC30, Optomed Aurora IQ 50-degree 5 Mpix, Heidelberg Spectralis ONH-RC/PPole-H/macular OCTA, Topcon Triton 12.0x12.0 and 6.0x6.0 mm, Dexcom G6 at five-minute sampling, Garmin Vivosmart 5 at 5-second sampling, LeeLab Anura), which is study-manual level detail.

questions.applicability_evidence: Evidence of human participants outside Q8's own fields: description states the dataset was 'collected from individuals with and without T2DM' across three sites with 'Version 3.0.0 contains data from 2280 participants'; collection_mechanisms describes participant-facing procedures (REDCap questionnaires, monofilament testing, MoCA administered on an iPad, 10-day wear of a Dexcom G6 and Garmin Vivosmart 5); collection_timeframes and data_collectors describe recruitment and enrollment by clinical research coordinators.

Absent: data_protection_impacts, with no DPIA statement anywhere in the record.

Sibling AI_READI records on the same bundle carry the source's 'no data protection impact analysis has been conducted' as a truthful negative, so the omission is a run-level gap rather than a source limitation. questions.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared and available for reuse: distribution_formats is populated with four formats and media types; page 'https://fairhub.io/datasets/3' and data_governance.access_review_process 'https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access' give an accessible route; the licence expressly grants download, reproduction and derivative-work rights for research and commercial purposes.
questions.description: Standard formats, ontologies, schema conformance, cross-platform linkage, integration capability
questions.score_label: Standard formats + schema/ontology compliance + integration capability
questions.evidence: conforms_to describes the Clinical Dataset Structure v0.1.1 hierarchy and names WFDB, OMOP CDM, DICOM, Open mHealth and the NASA ASCII/ESDS guidelines per data type, plus RO-Crate 1.2-DRAFT with the FAIRscape profile 0.1 and one subcrate per data type; conforms_to_standard carries seven controlled values including RO_CRATE; conforms_to_schema 'https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema' with conforms_to_class 'Dataset'. Every file_collection repeats its own conforms_to and conforms_to_standard. Integration capability: participant-ID directories in every data type and modality ('a participant's records can be linked across modalities'), participants.tsv carrying the recommended split assignment, dqd_omop.json for OMOP CDM Data Quality Dashboard analysis, RxNorm codes in the medications log, ICD-10 codes in the recruitment screen, and related_datasets with three typed relations (two is_new_version_of, one has_part).

OMOP CDM plus DICOM, WFDB and Open mHealth give real cross-dataset harmonization paths, the RO-Crate packaging adds a machine-readable exchange layer, and cross-modal linkage is stated concretely rather than asserted. file_collections.compression is unused, which is minor.

questions.name: Tool and Software Transparency
questions.applicability_evidence: external_resources names a code repository: 'GitHub organization of the AI-READI project — https://github.com/AI-READI'. purposes additionally identifies a reusable methodological output ('To create a model for developing large scalable datasets, sharing a blueprint that future data generation projects can follow').
questions.description: Preprocessing, cleaning, labeling strategies and the software tools used

Absent: labeling_strategies, machine_annotation_tools, annotation_analyses, imputation_protocols.

The point is withheld because no tool carries a version or a repository URL and the conversion pipelines the record itself describes name no software at all, which is the specific content the 5-anchor asks for.

questions.applicability_evidence: Evidence of human participants outside Q15's own fields: description ('collected from individuals with and without T2DM', 'data from 2280 participants'); keywords ('Diabetes mellitus', 'Eye exam'); collection_mechanisms (participant-administered questionnaires, monofilament testing, MoCA, 10-day device wear).
questions.description: Human subjects, demographic diversity, subgroup details
questions.evidence: instances: 2,280 'Individual study participant' entries with data_topic B2AI_TOPIC:43, label false, and two missing_information blocks (modality gaps with causes; sex, race, ethnicity and medications removed from the public release). subpopulations: four entries — self-reported race and ethnicity (380 Hispanic, 545 Asian, 519 Black, 836 White), biological sex (951 male, 1,329 female), diabetes status group with the four recruitment strata defined and counted (776 / 560 / 686 / 258), and age (eligibility 40 years or older with protocol maximum 85; mean 60.8 ± 11.3 years). splits: 1,576 / 352 / 352 assigned per participant in participants.tsv, balanced as far as possible for sex, race/ethnicity and diabetes status, with per-split mean ages. Inclusion and exclusion criteria appear in human_subject_research.special_populations and preprocessing_strategies (age 40+, consent capacity, English, not pregnant, no gestational diabetes, no type 1 diabetes). at_risk_populations and missing_data_documentation both populated.
questions.quality_note: Demographic characterization is complete on all four balancing dimensions, every count reconciles to 2,280, and the tension between recruitment-balance variables and their withholding from the public release is explained in the subpopulation identification text rather than left as a contradiction.

questions.name: Findability (Persistent Links)
questions.description: Persistent URLs for access and documentation
questions.evidence: doi '10.60775/fairhub.3' with id 'doi:10.60775/fairhub.3'; page 'https://fairhub.io/datasets/3'; access route 'https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access'; documentation 'https://docs.aireadi.org'; project site 'https://aireadi.org'; 'https://zenodo.org/communities/aireadi'; 'https://github.com/AI-READI'; licence DOI 10.5281/zenodo.17555036; publication DOIs 10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x and 10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449; registry https://classic.clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/show/NCT06002048.
questions.quality_note: A DOI-resolvable landing page plus documentation, repository, registry and publication links, with per-version DOIs for the whole release chain.

questions.name: Accessibility (Access Mechanism)
questions.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared and available for reuse: distribution_formats populated with four formats; page and data_governance.access_review_process give a documented public route; the licence grants download, reproduction and derivative-work rights for research and commercial purposes.
questions.description: How users obtain the dataset (download, DUA, login)
questions.score_label: Fully defined access path (platform, login, policy)
questions.evidence: data_governance.access_review_process: 'Accessing the dataset requires logging in through a verified ID system, agreeing to use the data only for type 2 diabetes related research, and agreeing to the license terms', with the FAIRhub access type recorded as 'PublicDownloadSelfAttestationRequired' and the conditions published at https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access. third_party_sharing: is_shared true, distribution through FAIRhub under DOI 10.60775/fairhub.3 subject to those three gates, with onward conveyance limited to identically bound licensees. distribution_formats: four formats with media types and the content each carries. license_and_use_terms sets the storage, security and secondary-sharing obligations a requester accepts. informed_consent.consent_scope and raw_data_sources.access_details distinguish the public release from the private/controlled version and from unreleased raw data.
questions.quality_note: Platform, authentication, attestation, licence assent and the published conditions-of-access URL are all explicit, and the public versus controlled tiers are distinguished. The dedicated download_url slot and distribution_formats.access_urls are unused, which costs nothing here because the access route is fully specified elsewhere.

questions.name: Reusability, Use Guidance, and Social Impact
questions.description: License clarity, use guidance, and social impact analysis
questions.score_label: License + comprehensive use guidance; social impact analysis thin
questions.evidence: license_and_use_terms: the full AI-READI Data License Agreement v2.0 terms with DOI, storage limits, derivative and synthetic data treatment, acknowledgement, NIH GDS compliance, termination and warranty disclaimer. intended_uses: two categories with usage_notes and an example — T2DM research with the attestation requirement, and research plus commercial AI/ML development with the model-distribution carve-out. prohibited_uses: six entries with reasons — no clinical treatment decisions, no re-identification or contact of subjects, no sharing with third-party model vendors for training or weight modification even under a BAA, no conveyance to non-licensees, no reproduction beyond small samples in up to five figures per paper, no removal of watermarking. future_use_impacts: one entry stating that no uses resulting in unfair treatment or other harms are currently anticipated, naming a theoretical future re-identification risk from AI inference of patient characteristics, and naming the dissemination system, the strict licence and watermarking of both public and controlled sets as the response. Absent: discouraged_uses.
questions.quality_note: Use guidance is comprehensive and licence-grounded, with the most specific prohibition list of any slot in the record. The social-impact limb falls short of the top anchor: future_use_impacts is a single entry opening with 'do not currently anticipate' and confined to re-identification, with no analysis of stigmatization or fairness risk from a non-representative cohort, and discouraged_uses is unused.

questions.name: Data Integrity, Provenance Graph, and Quality
questions.description: Version access, errata, updates, derivation, parent datasets, provenance
questions.score_label: Version history plus textual lineage; no structured provenance graph
questions.evidence: version_access (three DOI-bearing releases with counts, dates, accessibility and inter-version changes), updates (annual static releases, no in-place modification), distribution_dates (three release dates each tied to its DOI). raw_data_sources: EHR screening source marked as not released, and device-native exports naming each native format and its conversion target (.xml, .csv, .fda, .sdt, .FIT, DICOM), with a preservation and non-release rationale. preprocessing_strategies and cleaning_strategies carry the processing lineage with named agents (site principal investigator approval for edits, site data managers for QC before upload, central project team for standardization). related_datasets: two is_new_version_of relations to the predecessor DOIs and one has_part relation to the mini-subset with a caveat explaining why containment rather than derivation was chosen. missing_data_documentation, splits, anomalies, known_limitations and per-collection conforms_to support quality assessment. conforms_to records RO-Crate 1.2-DRAFT with the FAIRscape profile and one subcrate per data type. Absent: errata, was_derived_from, parent_datasets, subsets.
questions.quality_note: Entity–activity–agent lineage is recoverable from prose (device to native format to conversion to released directory, with the responsible role named at each step), which exceeds the version-history-only anchor. The top anchor is not met: the record itself presents no structured provenance graph, the RO-Crate that would carry one is referenced rather than reproduced, and the dedicated derivation slots (was_derived_from, parent_datasets) and errata are empty while their content sits in prose and in related_datasets.

questions.name: Bias Documentation and Responsible AI Alignment
questions.description: Known biases with standardized taxonomy and fairness analysis
questions.score_label: Biases categorized with taxonomy and mitigation; no AIO mapping or formal fairness analysis
questions.evidence: known_biases: four entries, every one carrying a BiasTypeEnum value — selection_bias (volunteer bias limiting generalizability), representation_bias (pilot phase not balanced, ongoing enrollment, no Pacific Islanders or Native Americans) with a mitigation_strategy naming triple-balanced recruitment targets, under/oversampling, three geographically distinct sites and balanced train/validation/test splits, sampling_bias (predominantly urban hospital-based recruitment) with a mitigation_strategy naming uniform protocols across sites and deliberate site selection, and a second selection_bias entry on the English-language eligibility requirement and its effect on Hispanic and Asian recruitment. future_use_impacts identifies the re-identification risk with its mitigations. known_limitations adds a representativeness_limitation with scope_impact and a scope_limitation covering the withheld variables. splits documents balanced validation and test sets 'intended to reduce disparities in models developed using this dataset'.
questions.quality_note: Taxonomy is applied systematically to every entry, which is stronger than prose-only bias notes, and the balanced-split design is a genuine fairness mitigation. Short of the top anchor: there is no AIO or CROISSANT RAI mapping, no fairness analysis with measured subgroup outcomes, and the fourth bias entry (English-language eligibility) carries no mitigation_strategy despite the record noting elsewhere that translation was not feasible.

strengths: Quantitative integrity: the ten file_collections file counts sum exactly to total_file_count 356,343, and every participant figure reconciles to 2,280 across race/ethnicity, sex, diabetes status and the recommended 70/15/15 split.
Collection protocol documented to device-model and parameter level across twenty mechanisms, with collector training, a Manual of Procedures and a three-practice-subject certification requirement.

Ethics coverage is specific rather than generic: IRB protocol number and approval date, reliance agreements, e-consent mechanics and withdrawal terms, a $200 stipend with its payment conditions, and explicit vulnerable-population negatives.

Source conflicts are declared rather than smoothed: institutional attribution, licence naming, enrollment start date, the file and byte count arithmetic, and the three competing de-identification statements are each recorded with the tier used to decide, in record-level and per-slot source_caveats.

Strong interoperability profile: seven controlled conformance standards including RO-Crate, per-directory conformance assertions, participant-ID linkage across every modality, and OMOP CDM tables with a data-quality dashboard file.
weaknesses: Only seven keywords, omitting the program identifier and five modalities the description enumerates, which is the single largest scoring gap against sibling records on the same bundle.
data_protection_impacts is absent with no DPIA statement anywhere, not even the truthful negative that sibling records carry.
No processing software carries a version or a repository URL, and the described conversion pipelines (.fda/.sdt to DICOM, .FIT to Open mHealth) name no tool at all.
The dedicated provenance slots are empty: parent_datasets, was_derived_from and errata are unused while their content sits in related_datasets, version_access and a variable quality_note.
Social-impact analysis is a single future_use_impacts entry confined to re-identification, with discouraged_uses unused and no fairness analysis beyond the balanced-split design.
recommendations: Extend keywords to at least eight, adding the program identifier (Bridge2AI, AI-READI) and the OCT, OCTA, FLIO, wearable activity and environmental sensing modalities the description already names.
Populate data_protection_impacts with the source's DPIA status, recording 'not conducted' explicitly where that is what the documentation states.
Name the conversion and QC tools with versions and link the specific AI-READI GitHub repositories, so that each described transformation has an agent.
Mirror doi:10.60775/fairhub.1 and doi:10.60775/fairhub.2 into parent_datasets and was_derived_from, and record the version 3.0.0 removal of the Snellen visual-acuity variables as an erratum.

Expand future_use_impacts beyond re-identification into a risk and mitigation analysis covering stigmatization and generalization failure from the non-representative cohort, and populate discouraged_uses from the stated limitations.
Document the funding continuation supporting activity past the 2025-08-31 project period and a preservation commitment that outlives the award.
